scenes.credit: launch film from @rauchg's post on X

steps.say: Every frame of this game is an X post. No browser drew any of them.

steps.caption: 241 frames in 260 ms, native Rust
steps.say: Two hundred and forty-one frames in two hundred and sixty milliseconds. This is xeet, a post renderer Guillermo Rauch released this week.

scenes.headline: How xeet draws a post without a browser
scenes.sub: and what pixel-perfect is checked against
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pica. Where a post's lines break is a browser's decision. xeet copies that decision instead of asking a browser to make it.

steps.say: First, X's own rules decide which text shows at all: hidden reply mentions, shortened links, and where Show more cuts.

steps.term: Chirp: X's typeface, split into subset files
steps.say: Every character then gets a face. One of twenty-eight Chirp files if it has the glyph, then Arial, Apple's emoji, and stand-ins for the Mac's fallbacks.
Each run is shaped by the Rust port of HarfBuzz, with advances converted the way Chrome converts them.
Then the line is fitted, exactly the way Blink fits it.
And it is painted with sixty-four sub-rows per pixel, and Apple's own emoji bitmaps.

params.snap: A width rounds up to the next 1/64 px before it is compared
params.reshape: Re-shaped on its own, the line no longer fits: step back a word

steps.say: Words go onto the line one break at a time. Each candidate end is measured, and the first one past the edge stops the search.

steps.term: Layout unit: one sixty-fourth of a pixel
steps.say: Blink counts in sixty-fourths of a pixel. A width is rounded up to the next one before it is compared.
A line one unit wider than its box still fits if it ends before a space, and not after a hyphen. The authors measured that on six hundred probes.
Then the line is shaped again on its own. Kerning across the break is gone, so it may not fit any more, and the loop steps back a word.

scenes.title: What it downloads, compressed
scenes.say: The engine is a module of under three megabytes over the wire. The fonts are the cost: one emoji pulls in Apple's emoji font, and the demo preloads every pack.

scenes.credit: X's embed and xeet, my screenshots

steps.say: Here is one post on two surfaces. On the left, X's own embed, in the system font with Twemoji.
On the right, xeet's timeline, in Chirp with Apple's emoji. Different sizes, but both cut the text at the same word.

states.say: To check line breaks, I rebuilt a Chrome oracle with Chirp loaded and compared fifteen layouts.
Fourteen matched. One did not: a Japanese post, eight lines in xeet and nine in Chrome.

left.title: xeet's own fonts
left.say: Handed xeet's own font files, Chrome agrees with it exactly.

right.title: This Mac's fonts
right.say: With the Mac's own fallback, the kanji come from a Chinese font, and one line is a third of a pixel too wide.

scenes.say: Pixel-perfect is a subscription, not a milestone.

scenes.text: xeet is Chrome's text arithmetic, copied and checked. Past Chirp and Apple's emoji, it depends on the Mac's fonts.
scenes.say: xeet is Chrome's text arithmetic, copied and checked. Past Chirp and Apple's emoji, the match depends on which fonts the Mac has.

recap: Matches Chrome when the fonts match
Use it to check drafts, not to embed
scenes.say: Blink's fitting, in Rust. It matches Chrome when the fonts match. Use it to check drafts, not to embed posts.
